correctness.rationale: Let H be the hyperelliptic pencil, so K=2H. An odd theta characteristic has an effective degree-two divisor D with 2D in |2H|. This linear system is the pullback of quadratic divisors on the base, so an odd D must consist of two distinct ramification points, rather than a fiber (which has two sections). This yields the Frobenius-equivariant 28 edges. For four edges, cancel pairs of ramification points using 2W=H and, when needed, complement the parity subset using the ramification divisor R∼4H. A parity subset of size two or four cannot give a divisor in |H| or |2H|, since those systems are pulled back and supported branch fibers have even multiplicity. Thus only empty or full parity subsets work, giving exactly the four-cycles or perfect matchings. My independent program generates these graph families directly and reconstructs cycle lengths by inversion from fixed counts of powers. It agrees with all 22 rows in the frozen CSV and recovers 21 full profiles, 18 four-count prefixes, 21 five-count prefixes, the unique collision in both components, and the sharp witnesses 7^45 versus 5^3 15^20. Distinct cycle profiles give distinct zeta functions by the same inversion. The two irreducible factor degree patterns exist over every odd field, and the explicit F3 examples' factors independently pass irreducibility checks. At line 26, 'torsor of odd theta characteristics' should read as a plane in the torsor of all theta characteristics, consisting of odd points; the odd locus itself is not a torsor. The proof via parity subsets is unaffected.
residual_risks: The 21 is an abstract spectrum over all 22 formal branch types, not an assertion that all occur over every small field. The cutoff five reconstructs the zeta function, not the branch profile.
